model.name: Ownership / Stewardship
model.purpose: Record who controls every meta-object: legal and beneficial title, fractional and joint holdings, fiduciary stewardship and custody, scoped delegation, capacity support or substitute decision, exclusive control of a unique record, restrictions that qualify title, and every transfer of control, without duplicating party identity, access grants, audit, licences or dispute procedure.
model.scope_statement: This mixin is the constitutional control register for other Vercy models. An access grant, disclosure shape or attestation is only meaningful when the issuer can be shown to hold, or lawfully exercise, control over the underlying object. Semantics are format-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and document stores are projections. Alignment with ISO 19152 LADM, UNCITRAL MLETR, W3C ODRL, W3C DID Core, DCMI terms, ISO 19115-1 CI_RoleCode, FATF beneficial-ownership guidance, FAO VGGT, the HCCH Trusts Convention and CRPD Article 12 is recorded as alignment, not claimed conformance. Identity prefers an authoritative master-system identifier, then a governed IRI, then a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID; a date is never an identifier. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
in_scope: Registry identity that makes a meta-object controllable, including singularity of the control record
Binding of one or more holders to that object, with basis of title and effective interval
Fractional, joint, several and survivorship holdings
Legal owner versus beneficial owner, nominees, bearer forms and control through other means
Public, private, communal, indigenous, customary and informal legitimate tenure claims
Trusts: settlor, trustee, beneficiary or purpose, separate fund and applicable law
Stewardship and custody without beneficial title, including ISO 19115 custodian versus owner
Exclusive control as the functional equivalent of possession, and identification of the person in control
Scoped, constrained, revocable mandates and sub-delegation
DID controller and DID delegate as operational cryptographic control, not legal title
Supported decision-making and substitute decision or guardianship, with safeguards and review
Voluntary conveyance and transfer of control, including conditions precedent
Succession on death, dissolution, office lapse or termination of a trust
Involuntary and exceptional effects: insolvency ring-fence, expropriation, abandonment, good-faith third parties
Rights, restrictions and responsibilities that qualify who may exercise control
Evidence, verification, discrepancy and currency of ownership data
Governing law, situs, jurisdiction and conflict-of-law constraints on the control relationship
out_of_scope: Natural-person identity, capacity facts as biographical attributes, and civil status (person model)
Organisation identity, officers as such, and corporate lifecycle (organisation model)
Access grants, ACLs, usage permissions and obligation evaluation as the authorisation layer (access-contract sibling)
Audit trails of reads and mutations (access-audit sibling)
Attestations, verifiable credentials and disclosure shapes as claims (attestation and disclosure siblings)
Court and dispute procedure; only the resulting transfer, restriction or annulment event returns here
Copyright and licence text, term and royalty schedules (intellectual-rights sibling); holder of rights remains in scope
Secured-credit terms, priority waterfalls and enforcement procedure (secured-transactions sibling); existence of a restriction on title remains in scope
Personal-data controller and processor determinations under data-protection law (privacy sibling)
Spatial geometry of land, assets or parcels (geospatial sibling)
Payment rails, consideration accounting and tax incidence
Cryptographic key material and DID document contents beyond the controller and delegate relation
Mineral, water and similar resource regimes that FAO VGGT explicitly leaves to other instruments

boundary_notes.distinction: LADM separates party, right, restriction and responsibility; this mixin records those distinct relations rather than collapsing them, but it is not a land cadastre and does not claim ISO 19152 conformance.
MLETR treats exclusive control as possession-equivalent without deciding beneficial title; possession-equivalence is stored here as its own predicate, not as ownership.
ODRL transfer is an action over an asset, not a land register; ODRL policies are the authorisation layer and are not title.
A DID controller is the party who can change a DID document; that is operational cryptographic control, not legal or beneficial title, unless an explicit bind is recorded.

boundary_notes.neighbor: DCMI Metadata Terms and ISO 19115-1 CI_RoleCode
boundary_notes.distinction: Both use rightsHolder for a party owning or managing rights, which conflates owner and steward; this mixin splits owning from managing and records the conflation as a conflict.
FATF requires both legal and beneficial owners to be visible; this mixin stores them as distinct relations and does not treat a local percentage threshold as the definition of beneficial owner.
HCCH trusts split legal title from beneficial enjoyment; the settlor, trustee and beneficiary relation is recorded here, while recognition remains non-universal under Articles 13 and 15.
CRPD Article 12 prefers support in the exercise of legal capacity over substituted decision; substitute guardianship remains recordable because domestic law still uses it, marked as being in tension.
Unregistered legitimate tenure is recorded as a claim class and is not converted into indefeasible registered title; VGGT is voluntary and nationally implemented, not self-executing title.

Matrimonial property, forced heirship, adverse possession doctrine, DAO personality, and digital-asset fiduciary statutes such as RUFADAA are jurisdiction-specific and are not universal classes in this mixin.

sources.title: The first five parts of LADM Edition II have been published — ISO 19152-1:2024 Geographic information — Land Administration Domain Model (LADM) — Part 1: Generic conceptual model
sources.organization: FIG / ISO TC 211 (LADM Edition II overview by standard co-editors)
sources.relevance: Describes ISO 19152-1:2024 Party package (LA_Party), Administrative package (LA_RRR specialisations LA_Right, LA_Restriction, LA_Responsibility, and LA_BAUnit), sources and versioned objects. Full ISO text is paywalled; this node is grounded in the published Edition II package description, not a claim of ISO-text transcription.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: W3C Recommendation. Defines Policy, Party function assigner/assignee, Asset, Permission/Prohibition/Duty, Constraint, uid as IRI, and top-level Action transfer as actions that involve the transfer of ownership to third parties.

sources.title: UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records (MLETR)
sources.organization: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law
sources.relevance: Official e-book text. Article 10: identify the record, keep it capable of control from creation until it ceases to have effect, retain integrity. Article 11 Control: exclusive control by a person and identification of that person; transfer of possession is met by transfer of control. Control is not defined because it is the functional equivalent of possession, which varies by jurisdiction. Substantive rights of the person in control remain other law.

sources.title: Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.1
sources.relevance: W3C Candidate Recommendation Snapshot 05 March 2026. DID controller: entity with capability to make changes to a DID document; a DID may have more than one controller; the DID subject may be a controller. DID delegate: entity granted permission to use a verification method, not necessarily to update the DID document. Controller is cryptographic and operational, not a statement of legal title.

sources.title: DCMI Metadata Terms
sources.organization: Dublin Core Metadata Initiative Usage Board
sources.relevance: DCMI Recommendation; also ISO 15836-2:2019 for the most useful /terms/ properties. rightsHolder: a person or organization owning or managing rights over the resource. rights, license, accessRights, provenance (changes in ownership and custody), mediator, creator, identifier, valid, coverage/jurisdiction.

sources.title: Guidance on Beneficial Ownership of Legal Persons (Recommendation 24)
sources.relevance: FATF, Paris, March 2023. Distinguishes legal ownership and beneficial ownership; ownership interests versus control/other means beyond a threshold; nominee shareholders and directors; bearer shares; adequate, accurate and up-to-date information; discrepancy reporting; access by competent authorities. Companion R.25 guidance on legal arrangements (trusts) published 11 March 2024 is in-scope as related FATF work.

sources.title: Voluntary Guidelines on the Responsible Governance of Tenure of Land, Fisheries and Forests in the Context of National Food Security — At a glance
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.relevance: Rome, 2012, ISBN 978-92-5-107305-6. Parent Guidelines endorsed by the Committee on World Food Security on 11 May 2012. Tenure: who can use which resources, for how long, under what conditions, via formal law or informal arrangements. Forms: public, private, communal, indigenous, customary and informal. States should recognise and respect all legitimate tenure rights, including informal; transfers and other changes (including expropriation) are a distinct part of the Guidelines.

sources.title: Convention of 1 July 1985 on the Law Applicable to Trusts and on their Recognition
sources.organization: Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH)
sources.relevance: Entry into force 1 January 1992. Article 2: settlor places assets under control of a trustee for a beneficiary or purpose; separate fund; title in the trustee; trustee has power and duty to manage, employ or dispose and is accountable. Articles 6–8 applicable law, including appointment, removal, delegation, security interests, duration, variation, termination, distribution and duty to account. Article 11 recognition and insolvency/death ring-fence. Article 15 mandatory other law: minors and incapable parties, marriage, succession, transfer of title and security interests, insolvency creditors, good-faith third parties.

sources.title: Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, Article 12 — Equal recognition before the law
sources.relevance: Adopted 13 December 2006, 2515 U.N.T.S. 3. Article 12: legal capacity on an equal basis in all aspects of life; States shall provide access to the support persons may require in exercising legal capacity; measures relating to the exercise of legal capacity shall provide appropriate and effective safeguards against abuse. This is the primary international-law counterweight to plenary substituted guardianship.

sources.title: ISO 19115-1 CI_RoleCode — function performed by the responsible party
sources.relevance: Defined values include owner (party that owns the resource), custodian (party that accepts accountability and responsibility for the resource and ensures appropriate care), rightsHolder (party owning or managing rights over the resource), mediator, originator, publisher, stakeholder. There is no code steward in this official 20-value list; stewardship in this mixin therefore aligns to custodian plus rightsHolder, not to a missing ISO role.

bundles.name: Tenure
bundles.description: Who presently holds control of a meta-object, on what basis, in what share, and whether that holding is legal title, beneficial enjoyment, or a legitimate unregistered claim.
bundles.rationale: Grouped because the presence of control must be established before its exercise, delegation or transfer can be evaluated: registration, title binding, shares and beneficial interest are successive layers of that one question.

layers.name: Registration anchor
layers.description: The identity event that makes an object a controllable unit rather than an ungoverned blob of bits or an unregistered social fact.

findings.name: Controllable registry entry
findings.description: A meta-object becomes operable as a control object only when it has a registry entry with a master-system identifier, an object kind, a registration basis and a registered time. LADM binds rights to a basic administrative unit, not to a naked spatial or digital artefact; MLETR requires the electronic record itself to be identified, kept capable of control until it ceases to have effect, and kept integral so that multiple claims to the same obligation cannot arise. DCMI identifier is an unambiguous reference within a given context and is not a date. Unregistered legitimate tenure remains recordable as a claim (see tenure-form-and-term) but does not by itself mint an indefeasible registered title.

questions.text: Which subject object, of which kind, is this registry entry the control unit for, and which master-system identifier is authoritative?
answer_data: object-reference: home-model IRI of the subject
registry-entry-id: master-system identifier; not a date

questions.text: On what registration basis was the entry opened, at what event time, and when was that fact observed or ingested?
answer_data: registration-basis: basis code or statute/instrument reference

questions.text: What reliable method identifies this record as the unique control object, keeps it capable of control until cessation, and preserves integrity against duplicate claims?
answer_data: singularity-method: method description or system identifier
integrity-criterion: how authorised changes are distinguished from alteration

questions.text: If no registry entry exists, is there a recorded legitimate unregistered tenure claim, and is it classified as a claim rather than as registered title?
answer_data: unregistered-claim-flag: whether a VGGT-style legitimate claim is asserted
claim-class: informal, customary, indigenous, communal, or none

data_elements.name: registry-entry-id
data_elements.description: Authoritative master-system identifier of the controllable unit; UUID or ULID only if the Dimension must mint one.

data_elements.name: object-kind
data_elements.description: Controlled kind of the meta-object (not a file type).

data_elements.name: object-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the subject object in its home model.

data_elements.name: registration-basis
data_elements.description: Legal or administrative basis on which the entry was opened.

data_elements.name: registered-at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 event time of registration with seconds and offset or Z.

data_elements.name: observed-at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 observation or ingestion time, recorded separately from event time.

data_elements.name: singularity-method
data_elements.description: Reliable method used to keep the control record unique and integral (MLETR Arts 10–11).

data_elements.name: ceased-at
data_elements.description: When the record ceased to have effect or validity, if closed.

artifacts.name: Registration source
artifacts.description: LADM-style administrative source (deed, filing, system record) that created the registry entry and supports chain-of-title reconstruction.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the issuing register, else governed IRI, else Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID; never a date.

layers.name: Title binding
layers.description: The current binding of holders to a registry entry, including tenure form, term and the ISO 19115 / DCMI distinction between owner, rightsHolder and custodian.

findings.name: Holder title record
findings.description: An ownership record binds one or more holder parties to exactly one registry entry, with a basis of title and an effective interval. ISO 19115-1 owner is the party that owns the resource; rightsHolder is the party owning or managing rights, which is a known conflation with stewardship; custodian accepts accountability without being the owner. DCMI creator, publisher and rightsHolder are not interchangeable. Holders are referenced into the person or organisation models; this mixin does not store biographical identity.

questions.text: Who are the current holder parties of this registry entry, and is each recorded as owner, rightsHolder, custodian or another CI_RoleCode?
What is the basis of title, from when is it effective, and is the binding current, superseded, disputed or annulled?
answer_data: effective-to: end or null if current

questions.text: Is the recorded holder distinct from the creator, publisher or originator of the object, and which identifiers prove that distinction?
answer_data: creator-party-id: DCMI creator or ISO originator if known, else null
distinction-evidence: how owner and originator were separated

questions.text: Who is authorised to read this title extract, and which competent-authority or holder-granted exception applies?
answer_data: access-exception: holder, delegate, competent-authority, or deny

data_elements.name: ownership-record-id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the current title binding.

data_elements.name: holder-party-ids
data_elements.description: Holder references into person or organisation models.

data_elements.name: holder-role-code
data_elements.description: ISO 19115 CI_RoleCode: owner, rightsHolder, custodian or other recorded code.

data_elements.name: title-basis
data_elements.description: LADM-style right type or instrument basis.

artifacts.name: Title extract
artifacts.description: Third-party readable current-holder extract for one named object, omitting full history, shares, mandates and guardianships unless requested.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived projection identified by the ownership-record-id it extracts plus the observation time of the extract; never a date alone.

findings.name: Tenure form and term
findings.description: FAO VGGT defines tenure as the rules that determine who can use which resources, for how long, and under what conditions, whether by written law or unwritten custom. Forms in scope are public, private, communal, indigenous, customary and informal. LADM right types are domain-specific specialisations of LA_Right and may be time-limited. DCMI valid records a validity interval. Informal and customary claims must be classed as legitimate tenure claims when asserted, without being rewritten as Torrens indefeasible title.

questions.text: Is this holding public, private, communal, indigenous, customary, informal or mixed, and who is the community holder if the form is collective?
From when until when may the holders use or control the object, and under what conditions?
Is this a registered title, a legitimate unregistered claim, or a contested claim, and which source supports that class?

data_elements.name: tenure-form
data_elements.description: public, private, communal, indigenous, customary, informal, or mixed.

data_elements.name: term-to
data_elements.description: End of term, or open if perpetual or unknown.

data_elements.name: community-holder-id
data_elements.description: Collective or community party if communal or indigenous.

artifacts.name: Tenure classification record
artifacts.description: Classification of tenure form, term and legitimacy class bound to the ownership record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the ownership-record-id it classifies plus the classification source; master-system identifier preferred, else governed IRI.

layers.name: Holding shares
layers.description: Partition of one title among co-holders, including joint versus several exercise and survivorship.

findings.name: Joint and fractional holdings
findings.description: A holding share records one party's fraction of a jointly held object. LADM Edition II retains the party and administrative packages in which shares attach to rights on a BAUnit. FATF treats layered shareholdings, nominee shareholders and bearer shares as techniques that can obscure beneficial ownership, so a share record must state whether the named holder is a nominee and whether the instrument is immobilised. Fractions should sum to one unless an explicit open remainder or discrepancy is recorded. Joint versus several determines whether one co-holder may act alone. Survivorship is a succession rule, not an identifier.

questions.text: Which parties hold which fractions of this title, and do the fractions sum to one, leave an open remainder, or fail a sum check?
May any one co-holder exercise the whole right, or must they act jointly, and does survivorship apply?
Is any named shareholder a nominee, who is the nominator, and is a bearer form still outstanding?
answer_data: bearer-outstanding: bearer share or warrant still in issue

questions.text: When did the last share restructure occur, and which instrument authorised the change of fractions or parties?

data_elements.name: fraction
data_elements.description: Numerator and denominator or decimal with declared precision.

data_elements.name: survivorship-flag
data_elements.description: Whether the share accrues to remaining co-holders on death.

data_elements.name: nominee-flag
data_elements.description: Whether the named holder is a nominee.

artifacts.name: Share schedule
artifacts.description: Schedule of all current shares on one ownership record, with sum-check and nominee flags.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent ownership-record-id plus the restructure event time of the current partition; never a date alone.

layers.name: Beneficial interest
layers.description: Natural persons who ultimately own or control, as distinct from the legal owner of record, including control through other means.

findings.name: Legal versus beneficial ownership
findings.description: FATF Guidance on Beneficial Ownership of Legal Persons (March 2023) requires adequate, accurate and up-to-date information on both the legal owner and the beneficial owner. Beneficial ownership may arise through ownership interests or through control or other means beyond a percentage threshold. Layered legal persons, nominee shareholders and directors, unrestricted legal-person directors, and bearer shares are listed concealment methods. For trusts and similar legal arrangements, FATF Recommendation 25 and the HCCH Trusts Convention require the settlor–trustee–beneficiary split to be visible: legal title may stand in the trustee while beneficial enjoyment lies with beneficiaries. A percentage threshold used by one jurisdiction is not itself the FATF definition of beneficial owner.

questions.text: Which natural persons ultimately own or control this object or its holding vehicle, and through ownership interests, control or other means, or both?
Do legal owners and beneficial owners differ, and which nominees, layered persons or bearer forms sit between them?
answer_data: intermediary-description: nominee, layer or bearer description

questions.text: When was beneficial-ownership information last confirmed adequate, accurate and up to date, and is a discrepancy report open?
Which competent authorities, financial institutions or other lawful recipients may access this beneficial-ownership record, and at what cost or restriction?
answer_data: access-legal-basis: FATF R.24 access pathway as implemented locally

data_elements.name: beneficial-owner-party-ids
data_elements.description: Natural persons who ultimately own or control.

data_elements.name: interest-description
data_elements.description: How the BO interest is constituted, without treating a local percent threshold as universal.

data_elements.name: information-currency-at
data_elements.description: When BO information was last confirmed current.

artifacts.name: Beneficial owner declaration
artifacts.description: Declaration or registry extract of beneficial owners, control pathway, currency timestamp and discrepancy status.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the filing register, else governed IRI; superseding declarations are new serials, not overwrites.

bundles.name: Fiduciary stewardship
bundles.description: Control exercised for others: trusts, appointed stewards and custodians, and exclusive possession-equivalent control of a unique record, without conflating those roles with beneficial ownership.
bundles.rationale: Grouped because control held for another party — trust, custody, or possession-equivalent exclusive control — must stay separate from beneficial ownership rather than collapse into a single owner field.

layers.name: Trust arrangement
layers.description: Settlor, trustee, beneficiary or purpose, separate fund, applicable law, and ring-fence from the trustee's personal estate.

findings.name: Trust parties and separate fund
findings.description: HCCH Trusts Convention Article 2 defines a trust as a relationship created inter vivos or on death by a settlor when assets are placed under the control of a trustee for a beneficiary or a specified purpose. Characteristics: the assets are a separate fund and not part of the trustee's own estate; title stands in the trustee or another on the trustee's behalf; the trustee has the power and the duty, in respect of which the trustee is accountable, to manage, employ or dispose of the assets. Reservation of settlor powers, and the trustee also being a beneficiary, are not necessarily inconsistent with a trust. Article 11 requires that personal creditors of the trustee have no recourse against trust assets and that those assets do not fall into the trustee's insolvency, matrimonial property or death estate. The Convention applies only to voluntarily created trusts evidenced in writing (Article 3) and does not bind States to recognise trusts whose significant elements connect to non-trust States (Article 13).

questions.text: Who is the settlor, who are the trustees, who are the beneficiaries or what is the purpose, and is the trustee also a beneficiary?
Do the assets constitute a separate fund that is excluded from the trustee's personal, insolvency, matrimonial and death estates, and where is that ring-fence recorded?
answer_data: ring-fence-status: how Article 11 effects are recorded
asset-title-standing: in trustee name or nominee for trustee

questions.text: Which law governs the trust, was it chosen by the settlor or selected by closest connection, and is recognition refused under Article 13?
What powers and duties does the trustee have to manage, employ or dispose, to delegate, to create security interests, and to account, and how is the trustee removed?

data_elements.name: beneficiary-party-ids
data_elements.description: Beneficiaries, or empty if purpose trust.

data_elements.name: purpose
data_elements.description: Specified purpose if not a beneficiary trust.

data_elements.name: governing-law
data_elements.description: Law chosen by settlor or closest-connection law (Arts 6–7).

artifacts.name: Trust instrument
artifacts.description: Written instrument creating or evidencing the trust, including chosen law and trustee powers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the instrument register, else governed IRI, else Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID; variations are new serials.

layers.name: Steward and custody
layers.description: Appointed operators who accept accountability for an object without beneficial ownership, and exclusive control of a unique electronic record as possession-equivalent.

findings.name: Steward appointment and duties
findings.description: ISO 19115-1 custodian is the party that accepts accountability and responsibility for the resource and ensures appropriate care; owner is a different code; rightsHolder may own or manage rights. DCMI mediator mediates access; DCMI provenance records significant changes in ownership and custody. HCCH Article 2 gives the trustee power and duty with accountability, which is the fiduciary pattern this layer generalises to non-trust stewards (museum custodians, data custodians, court-appointed receivers recorded as effects). A steward is not a beneficial owner. Appointment has a basis, a duty list, a term and an accountability route. ISO 19115-1 has no code steward; this mixin must not invent that code as if it were ISO-canonical.

questions.text: Who is appointed to operate this object, for which holder, under which role code, and on what appointment basis?
What duties bind the steward, from when until when, and to whom must the steward account?
Does the appointment confer beneficial ownership, or only custody and care, and how is conversion of the asset into the steward's estate prohibited?
answer_data: beneficial-flag: must be false for a pure steward
non-conversion-rule: ring-fence or duty not to convert

questions.text: What significant changes of custody, as distinct from changes of ownership, are recorded for authenticity and integrity?
answer_data: custody-events: DCMI-style provenance of custody changes
observed-at: ingestion time of the latest event

data_elements.name: holder-party-id
data_elements.description: Beneficial or legal holder on whose behalf the steward acts.

data_elements.name: role-code
data_elements.description: custodian, rightsHolder-managing, trustee, receiver, or other declared non-ISO code marked as extension.

data_elements.name: appointment-basis
data_elements.description: Contract, statute, court order, or trust instrument.

data_elements.name: duty-list
data_elements.description: Duties including care, account, and non-conversion.

artifacts.name: Steward appointment instrument
artifacts.description: Instrument appointing a custodian or steward, listing duties, term and accountability route.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the appointing register or court, else governed IRI; re-appointment mints a new serial.

findings.name: Exclusive control of the record
findings.description: MLETR Article 11: where the law requires or permits possession of a transferable document or instrument, that requirement is met for an electronic transferable record if a reliable method establishes exclusive control of that record by a person and identifies that person as the person in control. Transfer of possession is met by transfer of control. Article 10 requires the record to remain capable of control from creation until it ceases to have effect, and to retain integrity. Control is intentionally undefined because possession varies by jurisdiction; substantive rights of the person in control remain other law. Singularity plus control is designed to prevent multiple claims to perform the same obligation. This is possession-equivalent control, not a determination of beneficial ownership, and it is in tension with LADM joint holdings and DID multiple controllers.

questions.text: Which person is identified as in exclusive control of this record, by which reliable method, and is exclusivity actually exclusive or a declared joint-control regime?
From creation until cessation, has the record remained capable of control, and has integrity been preserved apart from authorised changes?
Does the person in control hold legal title, beneficial ownership, a mere bailee's possession, or an undetermined substantive right, and which other law decides that?
When control last transferred, what event time and observation time were recorded, and did the transfer meet MLETR transfer-of-control equivalence?
answer_data: method-after-transfer: reliable method identifying the new person in control

data_elements.name: control-record-id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the unique electronic control record.

data_elements.name: person-in-control-id
data_elements.description: Identified person in exclusive control, or explicit joint-control regime identifier.

data_elements.name: joint-control-regime
data_elements.description: How joint control is represented if exclusive-flag is false.

data_elements.name: control-until
data_elements.description: End, or cessation of the record.

artifacts.name: Control proof
artifacts.description: Evidence that a reliable method currently identifies the person in exclusive control of the unique record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the control-record-id plus the observation time of the proof; the underlying record keeps its own master-system identifier.

bundles.name: Delegation
bundles.description: Control exercised by someone other than the holder under a scoped mandate, a DID delegate relation, or a capacity-support or substitute-decision arrangement.
bundles.rationale: Grouped because all powers exercised by a non-holder derive from, and are bounded by, a live parent title, whether their source is a mandate, a DID delegation or a capacity arrangement.

layers.name: Scoped mandate
layers.description: Revocable grants of specific powers from a holder or controller, with constraints, expiry and optional sub-delegation, never exceeding the parent title.

findings.name: Delegated powers and constraints
findings.description: ODRL models the assigner as the party issuing a rule and the assignee as the recipient. Permissions, prohibitions and duties may be refined by constraints, including temporal and spatial operands, and duties may be preconditions to permission. ODRL Agreement requires both assigner and assignee. HCCH Article 8(c) governs the trustee's right to delegate discharge of duties or exercise of powers. A mandate in this mixin is a scoped, usually revocable grant of named control powers from a holder (or trustee) to a delegate; it cannot exceed the live title it is issued under; sub-delegation is an explicit flag, not a default. ODRL policy uid is an IRI.

questions.text: Who granted which named powers over which object to whom, and under which parent ownership record?
What constraints limit the mandate, is it still unrevoked and unexpired, and may the assignee sub-delegate?
Do any granted powers exceed the live parent title, including after a transfer or restriction that narrowed the holder's own powers?
answer_data: narrowing-event-id: transfer or restriction that may have overtaken the mandate

questions.text: Before honouring an act, can a counterparty verify that the claimed powers exist, are in scope, satisfy constraints, and are unrevoked?
answer_data: verified-at: observation time of the check

data_elements.name: parent-ownership-record-id
data_elements.description: Title the mandate is issued under.

data_elements.name: constraints
data_elements.description: ODRL-style constraints: time, place, count, purpose.

artifacts.name: Mandate instrument
artifacts.description: Scoped grant of powers with constraints, expiry, revocability and sub-delegation flag, verifiable by a counterparty before honouring an act.
artifacts.identity_strategy: ODRL-style uid as a governed IRI, else master-system identifier of the issuing register; revocation never reuses the identifier.

findings.name: DID controller and delegate
findings.description: W3C DID v1.1 defines a DID controller as an entity that has the capability to make changes to a DID document. A DID may have more than one controller, and the DID subject may be a controller. A DID delegate is an entity to whom a controller has granted permission to use a verification method; the child in the specification's example may authenticate but not add devices without the parent's permission. This is operational cryptographic control. It is not legal title, not FATF beneficial ownership, and not MLETR exclusive possession of a transferable record, though an adopting Dimension may bind those relations together with explicit links.

questions.text: Which entities can currently make changes to the DID document, and is the DID subject among them?
Which delegates may use which verification methods, and are they forbidden to update the DID document?
Is this DID controller relation bound to a legal ownership record, and if not, has any agent treated cryptographic control as title?

layers.name: Capacity support
layers.description: Arrangements that support a holder in exercising legal capacity, or that substitute a decision-maker, with safeguards against abuse.

findings.name: Supported and substitute decision
findings.description: CRPD Article 12 requires recognition of legal capacity on an equal basis in all aspects of life, access to the support a person may require in exercising that capacity, and appropriate and effective safeguards against abuse of support measures. Traditional plenary guardianship is therefore in tension with the Convention even where domestic law still appoints guardians. HCCH Article 15 preserves mandatory forum rules on the protection of minors and incapable parties, so a trust or transfer may be blocked or reshaped by those rules. This layer records both supported decision-making agreements (the person remains the holder) and substitute arrangements (a guardian exercises the holding), with legal basis, scope, review date and safeguards. It does not store the person's medical diagnosis; capacity facts live in the person model.

questions.text: Is this arrangement supported decision-making, substitute guardianship, mixed, or minority parental authority, and who remains the holder of record?
Which holdings and decisions are in scope, which safeguards against abuse apply, and when must the arrangement be reviewed?
May the supporter or guardian execute a transfer of the principal's holdings, and is that authority derived from this arrangement or from a separate mandate?
Do HCCH Article 15 mandatory rules on minors or incapable parties, or a CRPD-implementing statute, constrain recognition of a related trust or transfer?
answer_data: mandatory-rule-hit: whether Art 15 or equivalent applies

artifacts.name: Capacity arrangement instrument
artifacts.description: Supported-decision agreement or guardianship order, with scope, safeguards and review date.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the ordering court or registering authority, else governed IRI; the principal is never identified by a date of birth.

bundles.name: Transfer
bundles.description: How control moves: voluntary conveyance, succession on death or dissolution, and involuntary or exceptional events, as recorded effects rather than as litigation procedure.
bundles.rationale: Grouped because every movement of control, bargained or not, rewrites or qualifies the same title records and must be stored as an effect on those records rather than as court procedure.

layers.name: Conveyance
layers.description: Voluntary transfers between living or existing parties, including conditions and transfer of exclusive control.

findings.name: Voluntary transfer of control
findings.description: ODRL defines transfer as a top-level action involving the transfer of ownership to third parties. MLETR Article 11(2) treats transfer of possession as met by transfer of control over the electronic transferable record. LADM records the administrative source of a change to an RRR. FAO VGGT Part 4 addresses transfers and other changes to tenure rights and duties, including markets. A transfer instrument names parties, the objects and rights conveyed, conditions precedent, execution time, and optionally a pointer to consideration in a finance model. Until conditions are satisfied, title does not rewrite. A completed transfer supersedes the prior ownership record; it does not delete history.

questions.text: Which parties conveyed which rights in which objects to whom, and under which instrument identifier?
Which conditions precedent remain, when was the instrument executed, when was that observed, and is title rewrite still blocked?
Did exclusive control of the electronic record move with legal title, only one of them, or neither, and is that split intentional?
If a transferor lacked capacity or is a ward, which arrangement authorised the conveyance?

artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the recording register, else governed IRI; each conveyance is a new serial and never overwrites the prior instrument.

layers.name: Succession and lapse
layers.description: Transfers that open on death, dissolution, office lapse, trust termination, insolvency ring-fence, expropriation or abandonment, as effects not as court procedure.

findings.name: Succession on death or dissolution
findings.description: HCCH Article 2 covers trusts created on death as well as inter vivos. Article 11(c) keeps trust assets out of the trustee's death estate; Article 15(c) preserves mandatory succession rules including indefeasible shares of spouses and relatives, so a testamentary transfer of a holding may be reshaped by forced heirship. Survivorship on a joint holding is a succession rule recorded on the share. Dissolution of an organisation holder is not modelled as person death; the organisation model supplies the dissolution event, and this mixin records the resulting opening of succession on the holdings. Digital-asset key control may not follow legal succession; that split must be explicit.

questions.text: What event opened succession on these holdings, when, and which former holder is affected?
Who are the successors, did survivorship apply, and do mandatory forced-heirship rules reshape the instrument?
Did operational cryptographic control follow the legal successors, remain with a surviving controller, or become irrecoverable?

data_elements.name: forced-heirship-flag

data_elements.name: crypto-control-split

artifacts.name: Succession opening record
artifacts.description: Record that a holder's death, dissolution or lapse opened succession on named holdings, with successor list if known.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the succession file, else governed IRI; the trigger event time is metadata, never the identifier.

findings.name: Involuntary and abandonment events
findings.description: FAO VGGT requires States to safeguard legitimate tenure rights against arbitrary loss including forced evictions, and treats expropriation among transfers and other changes. HCCH Article 11 ring-fences trust assets from the trustee's insolvency; Article 15(e)–(f) preserves insolvency-creditor protection and good-faith third-party rules, which may defeat a trust or a transfer. FATF notes misuse of corporate vehicles for sanctions evasion; a freeze or confiscation is an exceptional restriction or transfer effect. Abandonment, bona vacantia, escheat and adverse possession are widely attested in domestic law but lack a single global primary instrument in this source set; they are recorded only as jurisdiction-tagged exceptional events, not as universal classes. Dispute procedure itself belongs to the courts model; this finding stores the resulting effect.

questions.text: What exceptional event affected which holdings, what is the effect on title, and which authority ordered it?
In which jurisdiction is this event class recognised, and is it a universal mixin class or a tagged local doctrine?
Does a good-faith third-party or insolvency-creditor rule under HCCH Article 15 defeat or qualify this holding or this trust?

artifacts.name: Exceptional effect record
artifacts.description: Jurisdiction-tagged record of an involuntary or abandonment effect on title, pointing at the ordering instrument without storing court procedure.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the ordering authority's file, else governed IRI, else Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID.

bundles.name: Qualifications
bundles.description: Restrictions and responsibilities that qualify title, the evidence quality of ownership data, and the law and situs that govern the control relationship.
bundles.rationale: Grouped because restrictions, evidence quality and applicable law each qualify a title without being title, so a holding is never read as stronger than its burdens, its evidence or its governing law allow.

layers.name: Restrictions and responsibilities
layers.description: LADM restrictions and responsibilities, ODRL prohibitions and duties, and trust or public-law burdens that qualify who may exercise control without themselves being the credit agreement.

findings.name: RRR qualifications on title
findings.description: ISO 19152-1:2024 models LA_RRR as an abstract class with specialisations LA_Right, LA_Restriction and LA_Responsibility. A restriction or responsibility qualifies a title without transferring it. ODRL Prohibition disallows an action; Duty obliges an action; both may carry constraints and, for prohibition, remedies. HCCH Article 8(d) allows trustees to create security interests in trust assets under the governing law; Article 15(d) preserves mandatory rules on transfer of title and security interests. This mixin records that a restriction exists, who imposed it, what it forbids or obliges, its interval, and a pointer to any secured-transactions sibling for credit terms. It does not store priority waterfalls or enforcement procedure.

questions.text: Which restriction or responsibility qualifies this title, who imposed it, and what action does it forbid or oblige?
From when until when is the qualification effective, and which constraints refine it?
If this is a security interest, where do priority and enforcement live, and what is stored here besides existence of the burden?

data_elements.name: secured-transactions-pointer
data_elements.description: Sibling pointer for credit terms, else null.

artifacts.name: Restriction notice
artifacts.description: Notice that a named title is qualified by a restriction, responsibility, prohibition or duty, with interval and sibling pointer.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the noting register, else governed IRI; lifting a restriction adds a new serial rather than deleting the notice.

layers.name: Evidence and law
layers.description: How ownership facts are evidenced, verified and kept current, and which law and situs govern them.

findings.name: Ownership evidence quality
findings.description: FATF requires beneficial-ownership information to be adequate, accurate and up to date, with verification of identity and of BO status, and discrepancy reporting. LADM treats sources as first-class administrative objects attached to versioned rights. DCMI provenance is a statement of significant changes in ownership and custody relevant to authenticity, integrity and interpretation. Title quality is therefore an evidence attribute of a record, not a metaphysical property of the object: a Dimension may record registered, verified, discrepant, contested or unknown without claiming Torrens indefeasibility unless a jurisdiction instrument says so.

questions.text: Which sources support this title or beneficial-ownership fact, and what is their verification status?
Is this holding recorded as registered, verified, discrepant, contested or unknown, and has anyone claimed indefeasibility without a cited instrument?
What significant ownership and custody changes are needed to interpret authenticity and integrity of this object?

data_elements.name: indefeasible-flag

artifacts.name: Title evidence pack
artifacts.description: Bundle of sources, verification status, quality class and provenance statement for one ownership record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the ownership-record-id it evidences plus the verification observation time; sources keep their own identifiers.

findings.name: Applicable law and situs
findings.description: HCCH Articles 6–8: a trust is governed by the law chosen by the settlor or, failing that, the law of closest connection, ascertained especially from place of administration, situs of assets, residence of the trustee, and objects of the trust. Article 9 allows a severable aspect, particularly administration, to be governed by a different law. Article 15 lists mandatory forum rules that cannot be derogated from by voluntary act. DCMI coverage and Jurisdiction describe spatial applicability or the jurisdiction under which a resource is relevant. FAO VGGT is implemented through national strategies and legislation; it is not self-executing title. Lex rei sitae for tangible objects, lex societatis for legal persons, and chosen trust law may therefore diverge for one meta-object; the mixin records each pointer rather than picking a single world law.

questions.text: Which law governs this holding or trust, was it chosen or selected by closest connection, and what is the situs of the assets or administration?
Are administration or other severable aspects governed by a different law, and which mappings apply?
Which HCCH Article 15 mandatory categories (minors, marriage, succession, security interests, insolvency, good faith) override the chosen law for this object?
answer_data: effect: how recognition or transfer is constrained

questions.text: Through which national policy or statute, if any, are VGGT tenure principles applied to this object?

data_elements.name: choice-mode

artifacts.name: Governing law record

artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the holding or trust it qualifies, plus the instrument that made the choice of law; never a date alone.

composition.purpose: Every access grant must resolve its grantor against a live ownership record, mandate, stewardship charge or capacity arrangement in this mixin. ODRL permissions are the authorisation layer; they are not title. DCMI accessRights is not rightsHolder.

Reads of ownership and beneficial-ownership data, and all registry mutations, are logged in the audit sibling. FATF access pathways for competent authorities are an exception class, not a reason to skip audit.

Holders, wards, guardians, supporters, delegates, settlors, trustees, beneficiaries and beneficial owners who are natural persons are identified in the person model. Capacity facts as biography live there; this mixin stores only the arrangement that affects control.

Legal-person holders, corporate trustees, nominee vehicles and dissolved companies are identified in the organisation model. FATF basic company information and layered ownership sit across that model and this mixin.
Contested titles, contested successions and VGGT access-to-justice processes live in the dispute sibling. Outcomes return here only as transfer, restriction, annulment or quality-class events.

Licence text, copyright term and royalty schedules live in an intellectual-rights sibling. DCMI license and rights are pointers; rightsHolder remains here. ODRL transfer-of-ownership must not be read as a copyright assignment unless that sibling says so.

Priority, attachment, perfection and enforcement of security interests live in a credit sibling. This mixin stores only that a restriction exists on title, with a pointer. HCCH Articles 8(d) and 15(d) require that split.
Align to LADM party, RRR (right, restriction, responsibility), BAUnit, source and versioned-object packages. This mixin is not a land cadastre and does not claim ISO 19152 conformance.
Align exclusive control, singularity, integrity and transfer of control to MLETR Articles 10–11. Substantive rights of the person in control remain other law.
Align assigner, assignee, duty, prohibition, constraint and the transfer action to ODRL 2.2. Policies are not titles.
Align DID controller and DID delegate as operational control relations. Do not treat them as legal or beneficial title unless an explicit bind is recorded.

Align rightsHolder, rights, license, accessRights, provenance, mediator, identifier, valid and jurisdiction. Record the DCMI conflation of owning and managing rights as a conflict, not as a hidden identity.
Align owner, custodian, rightsHolder and mediator. There is no steward code in the official 20-value CI_RoleCode list; stewardship maps to custodian plus an explicit non-beneficial flag.

Align legal versus beneficial ownership, control through other means, nominees, bearer forms, currency and discrepancy. Do not treat a local percentage threshold as the definition of beneficial owner.
Align tenure pluralism, legitimate unregistered rights, associated duties, and transfer-or-expropriation effects. VGGT is voluntary and nationally implemented; it is not self-executing title.
Align settlor, trustee, beneficiary or purpose, separate fund, applicable law, ring-fence and Article 15 mandatory overrides. Recognition is not universal (Articles 13 and 15).
Align supported exercise of legal capacity and safeguards. Substitute guardianship remains recordable because domestic law still uses it, but it is marked as being in tension with Article 12.
Every registry entry extends the meta-object identity primitive; this mixin does not mint a second identity system.

owner_package_requirements: The owning package must name a root registrar that keeps the constitutional register of control and mints or binds master-system identifiers for registry entries.
The owning package must publish AGENTS.md with Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before serving any control record.

The owning package must route all reads of ownership and beneficial-ownership data and all registry mutations to the access-audit sibling as the system of record, keeping no second ungoverned log store.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Identifiers are master-system first, then a governed IRI in the owning Dimension's namespace, then a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID; a date is never an identifier. ODRL policy uid IRIs and DIDs remain in their issuing namespaces and are bound by explicit links rather than re-minted here.
registry_links: vr.wm-xct-001 — Ownership / Stewardship mixin registry entry
world.access-contract — authorisation layer that resolves its grantor here
world.access-audit — system of record for reads and mutations
world.person and world.organization — party identity for holders, trustees, stewards and beneficial owners

canonicalization_rules: Chain of title is append-only; current holder, current shares and current mandates are projections over it.
Event time and observation or ingestion time are stored separately in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; observation time is never used as event time.
patch_rules: Supersede current holders on a completed transfer or share restructure; do not mutate historical versions in place.
Revoke, expire, suspend or constrain mandates and amend steward duties and review dates as new states, retaining the prior state.
Reclassify legitimacy class (registered title versus legitimate unregistered claim versus contested) only with a new source, never by silent overwrite.
compatibility_rules: Alignments to LADM, MLETR, ODRL, DID, DCMI, ISO 19115-1, FATF, VGGT, HCCH and CRPD are alignments, not conformance claims.
Codes absent from an official list, such as steward in ISO 19115-1 CI_RoleCode, must be emitted as declared extensions and never as canonical values.

Legal owner, beneficial owner, custodian, person in exclusive control and DID controller are exchanged as distinct relations; a consumer that expects a single owner field must be given an explicit projection, not a merge.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier of the issuing register
Governed IRI under the owning Dimension's namespace
Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID when nothing authoritative exists
A date is never an identifier
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately for every control fact.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial instruments (registration sources, transfer instruments, mandates, appointment and capacity instruments, restriction notices, succession and exceptional-effect records) are named by the master-system identifier of the issuing register plus their own instrument identifier; superseding mints a new serial and never renames, reuses or overwrites a prior instrument.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: A mandate, stewardship charge, DID delegate relation or capacity arrangement MUST NOT confer powers beyond the live parent title; legal owner, beneficial owner, custodian, person in exclusive control and DID controller MAY differ and MUST be stored as distinct relations when known; a completed transfer MUST supersede current holders without deleting chain of title; fractions on one title MUST sum to one or carry an explicit open-remainder or discrepancy status; hard deletion of title history is forbidden except where a recorded retention rule and lawful erasure duty both apply.

policies: No access grant, disclosure shape or attestation is treated as issued by a grantor of record unless that party holds or lawfully exercises control under a live ownership record, mandate, stewardship charge or capacity arrangement in this mixin.

Delegated and fiduciary powers expire or shrink automatically when the parent title is transferred, restricted, annulled or ceases; counterparties must verify mandates against current title, not against the mandate instrument alone.
Legal and beneficial holders, custodians, exclusive controllers and DID controllers are recorded separately; collapsing them into a single owner field is a validation failure.
Chain of title is append-only. Current holder, current shares and current mandates are projections. Observation time is never used as event time.

Supported decision-making is the default classification when a CRPD-implementing basis is cited; plenary guardianship requires an explicit substitute mode, legal basis, scope, safeguards and review date.
Beneficial-ownership data is adequate, accurate and up to date, or it is marked discrepant or unknown; a stale BO record MUST NOT be presented as current.

read: Current-holder extract for the object holder, an unrevoked mandatee with extract power, or a logged competent-authority request.
Mandate verification result for a counterparty who presents a claimed act, returning pass, fail or indeterminate without dumping unrelated holdings.
Beneficial-owner resolution for competent authorities and other FATF access classes as implemented by the Dimension, always audited.
Chain-of-title reconstruction for a named object to a party who already has a legitimate interest in that object.
create: Registry entry that mints or binds a master-system identifier and records registration basis and event time.

Ownership record, share schedule, trust instrument, steward appointment, mandate, capacity arrangement, transfer instrument, restriction notice, BO declaration and exceptional-effect record, each with source-referenced provenance.
Succession opening record triggered by a person-death or organisation-dissolution event arriving from a sibling model.
update: Supersede current holders on completed transfer or share restructure; do not mutate historical versions in place.
Revoke, expire, suspend or constrain mandates; amend steward duties and review dates; update BO currency and discrepancy status; attach or lift restrictions.
Reclassify legitimacy class (registered title versus legitimate unregistered claim versus contested) with a new source, not by silent overwrite.
delete: Refuse hard delete of registry entries, title history, executed transfer instruments and succession files except under an explicit retention-and-erasure rule that names the lawful basis.
Allow logical cessation of a control record when it ceases to have effect (MLETR), retaining the cessation timestamp.
Erase or unlink personal identifiers only via the person-model retention interface; this mixin then stores a tombstone that a holder was present, not the biographical payload.

roles.name: Root registrar
responsibilities: Keep the constitutional register of control for the Dimension.
Mint or bind master-system identifiers for registry entries.
Refuse registrations that lack a source basis or that collide with an existing unique control record.

roles.name: Holder of record
responsibilities: Exercise or withhold control consistent with the recorded title, shares and restrictions.
Grant and revoke mandates that do not exceed the live title.
Appoint custodians without converting beneficial ownership.
Authorise access grants only while the holding is live.

roles.name: Steward or trustee
responsibilities: Operate the object according to the duty list and governing instrument.
Keep assets off the steward's personal estate.
Account to the named account-route.
Delegate only if the instrument allows.

roles.name: Mandate delegate
responsibilities: Act only within named powers, constraints and term.
Submit to mandate verification by counterparties.
Not treat a DID delegate relation as title.

roles.name: Beneficial-ownership examiner
responsibilities: Read legal-versus-beneficial pathways under a competent-authority or obliged-entity exception.
File discrepancy reports when legal owners, nominees and BO declarations do not match.
Never publish BO data through a current-holder extract.

roles.name: Capacity officer
responsibilities: Record supported-decision and substitute-decision arrangements with safeguards and review dates.
Block transfers that lack arrangement authority for a ward.
Flag CRPD tension when a plenary guardianship is filed.

access.default_rule: Deny all reads and writes of ownership, share, mandate, trust, BO, capacity and succession data except to the holder of record, a live mandatee with an explicit power, a steward within duty scope, or a named exception.
exceptions: Competent-authority access to basic and beneficial-ownership information as implemented from FATF Recommendations 24 and 25, always audited.
Counterparty mandate verification that returns only pass, fail or indeterminate plus the powers actually claimed, not the holder's full portfolio.
Court or dispute-resolution outcome ingestion that writes transfer, restriction or annulment events without opening investigative files in this mixin.

Public current-holder extract where a Dimension policy, VGGT transparency measure or land-register law requires publicity of legal owners; beneficial owners remain exception-gated unless local law says otherwise.
audit_requirements: Log every read of BO data, every title extract, every mandate verification, and every create, supersede, revoke or cessation event with actor, object, purpose, event time and observation time.
Forward those logs to the access-audit sibling; do not keep a second ungoverned log store as the system of record.
Retain audit records at least as long as the chain of title they explain, subject to person-model erasure duties which then require a tombstone rather than a silent gap.

coverage.claim: Wide-union mixin of meta-object control grounded in ISO 19152-1 LADM packages, UNCITRAL MLETR control, W3C ODRL transfer and assigner/assignee, W3C DID controller/delegate, DCMI rightsHolder and provenance, ISO 19115-1 CI_RoleCode, FATF legal-versus-beneficial ownership, FAO VGGT tenure pluralism, HCCH trusts, and CRPD Article 12. Alignment is not conformance. Completeness is falsifiable and jurisdiction-bounded.

checklist.notes: Master-system registry-entry identifier first, then governed IRI, then Dimension UUID or ULID; DCMI identifier; MLETR identification of the unique record; DID as operational identifier only. Dates are not identifiers.
Registration, current/superseded/disputed/annulled title, mandate offer/agree/revoke/expire, trust creation and termination, succession opened/completed, control until cessation, exceptional effects.

Title covers one registry entry; shares partition title; mandates issue under title; trusts split settlor/trustee/beneficiary; restrictions qualify title; DID controller/delegate; legal versus beneficial.
RFC 3339 event time and observation time; effective-from/to; mandate expiry; steward term; capacity review date; MLETR control from creation until cessation; DCMI valid.
LADM sources, DCMI provenance of ownership and custody changes, chain-of-title reconstruction, FATF currency and discrepancy.
This is the ownership mixin: legal title, beneficial ownership, custody, exclusive control, tenure form, trusts, mandates and succession.
Mandate cannot exceed title; share sum-check; BO discrepancy; singularity and integrity of the control record; ODRL constraint satisfaction on verify-mandate.
Default deny; holder, mandatee, steward and competent-authority exceptions; public legal-owner extracts only where law requires; BO gated.
Append-only chain of title; logical cessation; hard delete forbidden except named erasure duty with tombstone; person-model unlink rather than silent gap.
Alignments to LADM, MLETR, ODRL, DID, DCMI, ISO 19115-1, FATF, VGGT, HCCH, CRPD recorded as alignments; format-neutral; conflicts listed rather than papered over.
FATF R.24 legal versus beneficial, nominees, control through other means; HCCH legal title in trustee versus beneficial enjoyment.
CRPD Article 12 supported decision-making versus substitute guardianship, with HCCH Article 15 mandatory protection rules.
HCCH separate fund and ISO 19115 custodian versus owner; no ISO steward code.
MLETR Articles 10–11 exclusive control and singularity, marked in tension with joint holdings and multiple DID controllers.
VGGT public, private, communal, indigenous, customary and informal legitimate rights, including unregistered claims.

known_omissions: CIDOC CRM ownership and custody properties (P51, P52, P30) were not fetched as primary text and are not canonical here.
PREMIS preservation rights and agent roles were not fetched.
GDPR controller and processor are a data-protection sibling, not modelled as title; they were not fetched as primary support.
RUFADAA and other digital-asset fiduciary statutes are regional and omitted as classes.
UNIDROIT Cape Town Convention, UCC Article 9 and the Hague Securities Convention were not fetched; security-interest procedure is out of scope.
Social Tenure Domain Model (STDM) and continuum-of-land-rights graphics are secondary to VGGT and LADM and were not fetched.
Adverse possession, prescription, bona vacantia, escheat, community property and orphan-works regimes lack a single global primary instrument in this source set and are jurisdiction-tagged gaps.
DAO, smart-contract and non-person holders lack primary legal personality support here.
ISO 19152 full text is paywalled; Party and RRR structure is taken from the Edition II co-editor paper, not from a purchased ISO PDF.
ISO 19115-1 has no steward code; older profiles that listed steward are not used as if they were the current TC 211 list.
conflicts: CRPD Article 12 (legal capacity with support) conflicts with plenary substituted guardianship still used in many domestic systems; both are recordable, with substitute mode marked as tension.
DCMI rightsHolder and ISO 19115-1 rightsHolder mean owning or managing rights, which conflates owner and steward; this mixin splits them.
DID controller, MLETR person in exclusive control, LADM right-holder, FATF beneficial owner and HCCH trustee are five different control predicates; treating any one as the others is an error.
ODRL transfer of ownership is an action over an asset and is not a copyright assignment or a land-register conveyance unless a sibling says so.
MLETR exclusive control by a person conflicts with LADM joint holdings and DID multiple controllers; joint-control must be an explicit regime, not an implicit exception.
VGGT legitimate unregistered tenure conflicts with any Dimension rule that only a registry entry makes an object controllable; unregistered claims are a separate legitimacy class.
HCCH Article 13 permits non-recognition of trusts whose significant elements connect to non-trust States; trust records are not universally effective.
Bearer instruments remain possible under some substantive law (MLETR commentary) while FATF requires immobilisation or conversion; both facts must be visible.
FAO VGGT does not cover water and minerals; those resource regimes must not be smuggled in as tenure forms.
regional_assumptions: Torrens indefeasibility is a jurisdictional property, not a mixin default.
Common-law trusts are defined by HCCH Article 2; civil-law fiducie, treuhand and waqf are not assumed equivalent without an adopting-Dimension mapping.
Forced heirship and matrimonial property (HCCH Article 15) override chosen trust law in many civil-law forums.
Beneficial-ownership percentage thresholds (often 25 percent) are local implementations, not the FATF definition.
Publicity of legal-owner registers versus confidentiality of BO registers varies by State.
Guardianship of adults remains lawful in States that have not fully implemented CRPD Article 12.
Digital-asset succession without key recovery is operationally common and legally unsettled outside a few statutes.
adversarial_checks: If an agent issues an access grant from a party who is only a DID controller or only a custodian, the grantor-of-record check must fail unless a live title, mandate, stewardship power or capacity authority covers that act.
If a mandate still appears valid after the parent title transferred, verification must fail; powers do not float free of title.
If legal owner, beneficial owner and person in exclusive control are collapsed into one owner field, FATF concealment patterns (nominees, layers, bearer forms) become invisible.
If a Dimension treats VGGT informal tenure as a data-quality error, it will mint false unowned objects and invite eviction-like deletions.
If CRPD-implementing support is stored as guardianship, the principal is wrongly stripped of holder status.
If MLETR exclusive control is treated as beneficial ownership, bailees and system operators become false owners.
If ISO 19115 steward is emitted as a canonical code, the record is not aligned to the official CI_RoleCode list.
If chain of title is hard-deleted to satisfy a privacy request without a tombstone, both audit and succession reconstruction fail.
